packageRules.description: Let a crate release age a few days before proposing it: yanked or quickly-patched releases never reach a PR. 'strict' holds the branch back until the age is reached instead of opening it with a pending check.
ruma is re-exported by matrix-sdk; bumping it alone puts two ruma-common versions in the graph (see #104). Only bump the two together.

gtk-rs and the bindings built on it (gstreamer-rs, libadwaita, libshumate, sourceview5, glycin, aperture) all depend on one glib/gio version; bumping one alone either fails to resolve or puts two glib versions in the graph.
The LiveKit SDK and the libwebrtc bindings it pins move together.

Changes the MatrixRTC e2e harness exercises (the matrixrtc crate's own lockfile, the e2e stack's container images) may automerge only through Renovate itself, which waits for every check, the path-filtered 'MatrixRTC e2e harness' included. GitHub's native auto-merge only waits for required checks, and a path-filtered workflow cannot be a required one.

No check exercises a call inside the app itself, so the app's own matrix-sdk/ruma and LiveKit bumps (root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock) stop for a human; see docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, 'How we know an update works'.
publish-flatpak.yml only runs on release tags, so no pull-request check exercises a bump there.
